title: Eagles linemen Ojomo and Johnson scuffle during final preseason practice
dek: Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo and offensive tackle Fred Johnson engaged in a physical altercation during the 11th day of Eagles training camp on Thursday that included punches and a knee dive, escalating from an initial late shove. Coaches initially kept both in the drill; players and staff separated them after the fight intensified.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Ojomo and Johnson exchanged punches and Johnson was driven to the ground by a knee dive during team drills on the final practice before Philadelphia's preseason opener against Baltimore.
bottom_line: The scuffle occurred as both players were in competitive drills late in camp and did not result in immediate ejections from practice. Watch for any disciplinary action or practice restrictions announced in the coming days, and whether either player appears in the preseason opener against Baltimore.
body: Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo and offensive tackle Fred Johnson engaged in a physical altercation during the 11th day of Eagles training camp on Thursday during team drills, according to ESPN. The incident escalated from an initial confrontation into punches and a knee dive as the two separated, then collided again before players and staff intervened.

Ojomo took exception to a late shove by Johnson and squared up, looking ready to fight, per ESPN's reporting. Coaches decided to keep both players in for the next play after the initial confrontation. Johnson then blocked Ojomo to the ground and landed on him with his full weight. Punches were thrown before the two separated, but Ojomo dove at Johnson's knees, bringing the 6-foot-7, 326-pound Johnson to the ground, according to ESPN.

Players and staff jumped in to separate the two. General manager Howie Roseman, coach Nick Sirianni, and chief security officer Dom DiSandro gathered around Johnson to help calm him down. Roseman met with Ojomo before talking further with Johnson post-practice for about five minutes as the offensive lineman sat on blocking pads, per ESPN.

Team drills were halted after the fight and, after a group huddle to reset, the Eagles finished with a less competitive developmental period, according to ESPN. This was the last practice before the Eagles' preseason opener against the Baltimore Ravens.

Before Thursday's session, coach Nick Sirianni said, per ESPN: "I'm just so excited to see all the guys compete. At the end of the day, this business is for people that are ultracompetitive. And it's always good to go against somebody else. Sometimes at this point of camp, you're like, 'Man, I just want to hit somebody else and go against somebody else.'"
